scene: Ruth had waited twenty minutes at the post office to mail a birthday parcel to her nephew in Izmir. Taped above the counter was a printed notice: 'New customs declaration format since March. Staff can assist.' When her number was called, the clerk, Callum, turned the box over and said, loud enough for the queue to hear, 'This form is filled out wrong. Half of it is blank.' He slid the parcel back toward her and was already tapping the screen for the next number. At the next window, an elderly woman asked whether they still sold the stamps with lighthouses. Behind Ruth, a man in a cycling jacket checked his watch and muttered, 'Here we go.' Ruth stood holding the form, her ears turning red.
question: What will Ruth do next to maintain emotional stability?

options.A: Ask the elderly woman at the next window where the lighthouse stamps are sold, so she can buy a few to decorate the birthday box.
options.B: Tell Callum in front of the whole queue that he has no right to talk to customers like that, and refuse to step aside until a manager comes.
options.C: Remind herself that the form changed only recently and many people miss parts of it, take a slow breath, and ask a staff member to walk her through it.
options.D: Pick up the parcel without a word, walk out of the post office, and decide to just send her nephew some money online this year instead.

scene: At the children's hospital fundraiser, Margaret had donated a quilt she spent all winter sewing for the silent auction. One held up her phone to the other, they whispered, and both laughed before drifting toward the dessert table. Margaret, refilling the pen cups nearby, watched them go. Across the room, a waiter knelt to gather a dropped stack of napkins. Earlier, the organizer Ewan had told the volunteers that at last year's event most bids landed in the final fifteen minutes. Now he tapped the microphone and announced that the auction would close soon.
question: What will Margaret do next to maintain emotional stability?

options.A: Walk over to the two guests at the dessert table and ask them pointedly what exactly they found so funny about her quilt.
options.B: Quietly carry the quilt to the storage room, tell Ewan it no longer fits the auction, and stay out of sight all evening.
options.C: Tape a fresh bid page under the spa weekend's full sheets so later guests have room to write, then refill the remaining pen cups.
options.D: Remind herself that most bids come near the end and the laughter may have been about the phone, then breathe slowly and keep refilling pens.

subcategory: Test of Emotion Comprehension: Emotion Regulation
scene: Oliver has been an apprentice at Catriona's bakery on Mill Street for three weeks. This morning he baked his first tray of cardamom buns without any help. Catriona broke one open, chewed slowly, and put the tray on the back shelf instead of in the display case. Then she leaned toward Fraser, a regular who was paying for his rye loaf, and said something too quietly to hear. Fraser glanced over at Oliver and chuckled. By the door, a little girl asked her father whether the muffins had blueberries or raisins in them. Catriona wiped her hands on her apron and told Oliver, 'Stay twenty minutes after closing today. question: What will Oliver do next to maintain emotional stability?

options.A: Walk up to the counter and ask Catriona, in front of the waiting customers, why she and Fraser were laughing at his buns.
options.B: Tell himself Catriona asked for the recipe card so she can coach him, and jot down which steps he was unsure about.
options.C: Tell Catriona he has a dentist appointment this afternoon and slip out before closing so the talk about the buns never happens.
options.D: Quickly bake a second tray of buns with double the cardamom and slide it into the display case before Catriona notices.

subcategory: Test of Emotion Comprehension: Emotion Regulation
scene: Lydia is pitching her food-delivery startup to three investors in a glass-walled conference room. Halfway through, Colm, the lead investor, raises a hand at the market-size slide. "These numbers look like guesswork," he says, loud enough that the associate by the door stops typing. Another investor, Beatrice, leans toward him and murmurs something, and both glance at the screen. Lydia turns to the projection and sees that the bottom line of her slide, where the survey source and sample size are listed, is cut off by the edge of the projector frame. Her co-founder Reuben, at the side table, quietly opens the full deck on his laptop. Outside the glass, a receptionist wheels a cart of coffee cups past the door. The timer on the table shows eight minutes left.
question: What will Lydia do next to maintain emotional stability?

options.A: Pause for a breath, tell herself the doubt probably comes from the hidden line, and explain where her figures came from.
options.B: Tell Colm sharply that he should have read the full deck before calling her numbers guesswork in front of everyone in the room.
options.C: Say nothing about the comment, skip quickly past the market slide, and rush through the remaining sections before the timer runs out.
options.D: Ask Reuben to email the investors a cleaner, reformatted version of the deck after the meeting so the slides look more polished.

subcategory: Test of Emotion Comprehension: Emotion Regulation
scene: Isaac works weekends at a small secondhand bookshop. Last Saturday he talked a regular customer, Benoît, into buying a thick crime novel, calling it the best book he had read all year. Behind the till, Isaac's handwritten staff-pick card for the same novel still leaned against a stack of copies. Next to it was a note from the owner saying the title had sold out twice last month. Across the shop, the owner, Ursula, was on the phone arguing with a delivery driver about a missing box of atlases.
question: What will Isaac do next to maintain emotional stability?

options.A: Tell Benoît in front of the queue that he probably skimmed the book and that his taste in crime fiction has always been predictable.
options.B: Leave the till and help Ursula with the missing atlases by phoning the delivery company himself to get a tracking number.
options.C: Pull the staff-pick card off the stack, push it into a drawer, and stop recommending books to anyone for the rest of the shift.
options.D: Remind himself that the novel sold out twice last month, so one reader disliking it is a matter of taste, and then serve the next customer.

question: How can Gareth persuade Zoé to take the market lane shortcut?

question: How can Leah persuade Yves to enter the blitz tournament with her?
